title: Edgecase ask mapping and prototype notes
content:
One-page working synthesis of oddball customer asks we keep seeing (July 2024)

Context: quick capture after two weeks of CS triage. These are not the top-volume asks, but they surface repeatedly across customers and often require engineering changes or product policy clarity. This doc is meant to: 1) map patterns, 2) propose small probes/prototypes to validate impact, 3) provide an initial engineering/ops cost estimate and rollback plan.

High-level summary:
- Pattern A: multi-turn hallucination corrections requested as a runtime feature (customers want server-side "local re-eval" or automatic consistency checks).
- Pattern B: deterministic fallback routing for high-latency model timeouts (prefer a cheaper but stable variant rather than retrying the same expensive model).
- Pattern C: developer ergonomics around per-request caching hints (customers want more granular control vs. global caching policies).
- Pattern D: token-accounting transparency for chained calls / tool-calling flows (billing confusion + unexpected spikes).

Representative quotes (annotated):
- "We saw the assistant contradict itself halfway through the long doc export — would be amazing if it flagged contradictory sentences automatically." — Platform eng lead, fintech 
- "When our high-quality model times out, the fallback arrives but is so different we have to reject the result — can we pick a fallback that preserves style/temperature?" — NLP product manager, edtech
- "Our caching needs to respect user-intent flags — caching a draft reply is bad; caching an idempotent classification call is fine." — Integrations engineer, marketplace

Synthesis and root causes (working hypotheses):
- Hallucination-correct requests often stem from customers needing a cheap, deterministic post-pass (syntactic/consistency checks) rather than retraining or full eval infrastructure. This feels like a product-level transformation (a lightweight "sanity pass" with heuristics + model check).
- Fallback mismatch is both a routing policy (which model variant to pick) and an evaluation mismatch: fallback models are optimized for BLEU/coverage rather than style alignment.
- Per-request caching hints are a missing knob in Redwood Optimize and Dedicated configs; current TTL and prefix caching are blunt instruments. Engineering fears: abuse vector if hints are misused to sidestep rate limits or K-anonymity policies.
- Billing surprises mostly come from synchronous tool chains where token counts are additive and customers don't get an easy per-route breakdown. We have the telemetry but not a dev-friendly presentation or guardrails.

Proposed microfeatures / probes (fast, 2–6 week cycles):
1) "Sanity pass" prototype (2 wks): small server-side pipeline that runs 1–2 heuristic checks after generation: contradiction detector (embedding-based), numeric consistency (regex/parse), and short style-preservation metric. Output: pass/fail + 1-line rationale. Scope: hosted API only, opt-in flag. Success metric: reduction in "contradiction" CS tickets for pilot customers by 40% in 30 days.
   - Engineering notes: can be implemented as a lightweight synchronous sidecar using an off-the-shelf contrastive embedder. Cost: ~0.5x extra CPU per request in worst case. Rollback: disable flag.
2) Deterministic-fallback routing rule (3–4 wks): add routing policy type "style-preserving fallback" that picks fallback model based on a small style-distance measure computed from prompt+context. Pilot on Dedicated and Hosted.
   - Risk: extra compute to score candidate fallbacks; mitigation: precompute fingerprints for common fallbacks and only compare fingerprint at runtime.
3) Per-request caching control (2–3 wks): introduce hint headers: X-Redwood-Cache: no-cache | idempotent | ephemeral. Map idempotent -> allowed TTL > default; ephemeral -> no caching; default -> existing behavior. Provide guardrails in Console for admins to limit usage.
   - Security note: audit tokens and rate-limit bypass when hints used — require role-based enablement for orgs.
4) Token-breakdown mini-dashboard (3 wks): show per-invocation token splits for chained calls and tool outputs, with an expandable view that maps to billing. Quick win: surface largest contributing segment and a "preview optimize tips" row.

Prioritization and expected impact (customer-value vs engineering-effort):
- Sanity pass: High value, low-medium effort. Good for fintech/healthcare regulated customers.
- Fallback routing: Medium-high value, medium effort. Prevents customer-level rollbacks and trust issues.
- Cache hints: Medium value, low effort (but policy complexity). Enables customers with hybrid workloads (batch + real-time).
- Token dashboard: High value for billing clarity, low effort (UI + telemetry join).

Open questions / unknowns (for follow-up):
- Which customers would be willing to run pilot flags in production? (CS to identify top 8 customers across tiers)
- For sanity pass: acceptable false-positive rate? Will users prefer a strict block or a soft warning?
- For caching hints: how granular should the hint scope be (per-route vs per-request vs per-organization default)?

Implementation sketch / tickets to spin up:
- Prototype: sanity-pass-service (server-side) -> PR at prototypes/pull/88; task: implement contradiction detector + numeric parser. Owner: eng-sre + applied-ml.
- Routing rule: add policy enum + scoring function -> JIRA: CS-RTX-201 (placeholder), owner: serving-runtime.
- Cache hints: API header design + console controls -> JIRA: DEVOPS-998, owner: console-and-tooling.
- Token dashboard: join view + CTA -> PM ticket: PD-1342, owner: product-hosted-api.

Quick checklist for pilot prep (CS + Solutions Eng):
- [ ] Identify 3 pilot customers and get opt-in confirmation. Target: one fintech, one marketplace, one edtech.
- [ ] Create Confluence pilot page and invite eng leads.
- [ ] Draft customer-facing release note wording (short blurb + opt-in instructions).
- [ ] Build telemetry markers for pilot to measure pass/fail and ticket drop-off.

Notes-to-self (raw fragments):
- Might fold sanity-pass into Optimize as a "quality guardrail" feature? But that leaks concept between product lines. 
- Watch for regulatory requirement patterns (financial reports) — those customers will prefer blocking vs advisory.
- Could we compress fallback fingerprinting by hashing prompt embedding + deterministic style vector? cheap but needs robust collision analysis.

Next steps (this doc):
- CS: collect pilot opt-ins by 2024-07-26.
- Eng/Product: quick feasibility sync 2024-07-22 (30m).
- Owner: Maya Chen to coordinate pilot deck and send to Liam and Sara.
